cases.about: Every receipt verifies against the pinned key, and the log still holds what both published checkpoints vouched for.
cases.name: level-2

cases.about: A sound chain with a pinned key, but nothing outside the machine says how long the log was.
cases.name: no-published-checkpoints

cases.about: A sound chain and published checkpoints, but the only key is the one in the log directory.
cases.name: no-pinned-key

cases.about: The last two receipts were removed. What is left verifies, but a published checkpoint vouched for four.
cases.name: tail-deleted

cases.about: The log and its checkpoints were signed again with a different key, which replaced public.key. It verifies on its own terms, not against the pinned key.
cases.name: rewritten-with-another-key

cases.about: The log was signed again with a different key. The only published checkpoint is the pinned key's, from when the log was empty, so it vouches for nothing; the receipts still have to verify against the pinned key.
cases.name: rewritten-after-an-empty-checkpoint

cases.about: The latest published checkpoint was signed by a key other than the pinned one.
cases.name: checkpoint-from-another-key

cases.about: The key holder changed the last outcome from pass to fail and signed it again. The chain verifies, but the receipt at the published head is not the one signed for.
cases.name: last-receipt-rewritten

cases.about: The signature on receipt 1 has one hex digit changed.
cases.name: bad-signature

cases.about: Receipt 1's target was changed and its old signature kept.
cases.name: edited-without-signing

cases.about: Receipt 2 names the genesis hash as prev and is signed with the right key.
cases.name: broken-link

cases.about: Receipt 2 was removed from the middle, so the receipt at position 2 says seq 3.
cases.name: receipt-removed

cases.about: Receipt 3's signature is written in uppercase hex. The bytes are the same, but only lowercase is accepted, so each receipt has one encoding.
cases.name: uppercase-hex-signature

cases.about: Receipt 0 says v 2, and the chain is rebuilt and signed after it.
cases.name: unknown-version

cases.about: Receipt 1 carries a field the format doesn't define, added after it was signed.
cases.name: unsigned-field-added

cases.about: Receipt 1 says "verification": null, added after it was signed. Absent optional fields are left out, never written as null.
cases.name: null-verification-added

cases.about: Receipt 1's decision says "review": false, added after it was signed. review is written only when true.
cases.name: false-review-added

cases.about: Receipts 0 and 1 were closed into a segment behind the checkpoint at 2; receipts.jsonl holds 2 and 3. The chain runs on across the files.
cases.name: segments-pinned-and-published

cases.about: Every closed segment was archived, so receipts.jsonl alone remains. It starts at its first receipt, 2, where a signed checkpoint vouches for the log.
cases.name: segments-all-archived

cases.about: Every closed segment was archived and no checkpoint vouches for the log at 2, where what remains starts.
cases.name: segments-oldest-archived-without-checkpoint

cases.about: The segment ends after 2 receipts but no checkpoint has count 2.
cases.name: segment-not-closed

cases.about: The segment holding receipt 2 is gone: the one before ends at 2, the next is named 3.
cases.name: segment-missing-between

cases.about: The receipts run on unbroken, but the second segment is named 3 while the first ends at 2, so its name and its content disagree.
cases.name: segment-named-at-the-wrong-start

cases.about: Every closed segment was archived, and two checkpoints signed with the log's key vouch for different heads at 2, where what remains starts.
cases.name: segments-conflicting-checkpoints

cases.about: The segment is named 0.jsonl instead of 20 digits, so a verifier can't tell where it sits.
cases.name: segment-misnamed

cases.about: Receipt 4 records a person extending a remediation plan: a person object, no verification, decision by human and tool mohar.
cases.name: person-receipt

cases.about: Receipt 4 says "person": null in place of the person object it was signed with.
cases.name: null-person-added

cases.about: Receipt 4's person object says "lesson": null, added after it was signed. Absent optional fields are left out, never written as null.
cases.name: null-lesson-added

cases.about: Receipt 4's person object carries a field the format doesn't define, added after it was signed.
cases.name: unsigned-person-field-added

cases.about: Receipt 5 is an escalation whose decision names the two people it was routed to; receipt 6 records one of them refusing it.
cases.name: escalation-names-approvers

cases.about: Receipt 6 was signed without "to"; an empty list is added after. An empty list is written by leaving the key out, so this is a second spelling a parser that reads it as absent would let through unsigned.
cases.name: empty-to-added

cases.about: Receipt 5's "to" names someone else after it was signed.
cases.name: approver-swapped

cases.about: Receipt 5's "to" is a string, not a list of strings.
cases.name: to-not-a-list

cases.about: Receipt 8 is a person's verdict on decision 7, naming who reviewed it and the seconds they spent.
cases.name: human-outcome-names-reviewer

cases.about: Receipt 8's "reviewer" is replaced by null after it was signed.
cases.name: null-reviewer-added

cases.about: Receipt 8 names a different reviewer after it was signed.
cases.name: reviewer-swapped

cases.about: Receipt 8's review_secs is lowered after it was signed.
cases.name: review-time-shortened

cases.about: Receipt 9 was allowed by a model answering for one person, whom its decision names.
cases.name: predicted-answer-names-person

cases.about: Receipt 9 names someone else as the person whose answer was predicted after it was signed.
cases.name: predicted-person-swapped

cases.about: Receipt 9's "to" is removed after it was signed, hiding whose answer was predicted.
cases.name: predicted-person-dropped

cases.about: Receipt 10 was held because the person it would have gone to had used up their hourly budget.
cases.name: held-request-names-who-was-full

cases.about: Receipt 10 names someone else as the person who was full after it was signed.
cases.name: held-person-swapped

cases.about: Receipt 10's result is changed to allow after it was signed.
cases.name: held-turned-into-allow

cases.about: Receipt 11 is a reviewer's accept and receipt 12 is another person's re-check of it.
cases.name: recheck-of-an-accept

cases.about: Receipt 12's of is changed to another receipt after it was signed.
cases.name: recheck-pointed-elsewhere

cases.about: Receipt 12's kind is changed from recheck to human after it was signed.
cases.name: recheck-turned-into-human-outcome

cases.about: Receipt 12 names the first reviewer as the re-checker after it was signed.
cases.name: recheck-reviewer-swapped

notes: Seeds are bytes 0x00..0x1f (the log's key) and 0x20..0x3f (another key), for testing only. Each case is a log: log_key is public.key in the log directory, pinned_key is the key the verifier was given some other way (null if none), published_checkpoints were kept outside the machine. A rotated log also has segments (file name under segments/ and its receipts, oldest first) and local_checkpoints (checkpoints.jsonl in the log directory); receipts is then receipts.jsonl. A verifier must report expect_level. Level 3 has no cases yet.
